2.6 Summary
Assuming that holdings of real money balances yield direct utility is a means of
ensuring a positive demand for money so that, in equilibrium, money is held and
has value. This assumption is clearly a shortcut; it does not address the issue of whymoney yields utility or why certain pieces of paper that we call money yield utility
but other pieces of paper presumably do not.
The Sidrauski model, because it assumes that agents act systematically to maxi-
mize utility, allows welfare comparisons to be made. The model can be used to assess
the welfare costs of inﬂation and to determine the optimal rate of inﬂation. Fried-
man’s conclusion that the optimal inﬂation rate is the rate that produces a zero nom-
inal rate of interest is quite robust (see chapter 4).2.6 Summary 75
